We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps enumerated forward: 1) Carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) Sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse order: start from target, break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline? Actually target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to aromatic ring (para to methyl). That's a sulfonamide linking aromatic amine to sulfonyl group attached to second aromatic ring. So retrosynthesis: disconnect sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (Ar-NH2). Then disconnect amide: the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So break amide to give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (aniline with NH2). Then disconnect α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid via Doebner modification (reverse: α,β-unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid). Actually forward Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retrosynthetic: α,β-unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid.

Thus three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (reverse: sulfonyl chloride + aniline). 2) amide coupling (reverse: carboxylic acid + aniline). 3) Doebner modification (reverse: α,β-unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid). So we need templates for each. We have template 401931 which seems to be amide formation? It shows amide product with C=C and carboxylate? Actually template: [#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>... This is reverse of amide formation? The forward direction (right to left) is amide + alkene? The template seems to convert amide with alkene to something else. Might be the amide formation step we need. We can use it.

We also need sulfonamide formation template. Search maybe for sulfonyl chloride to sulfonamide. Let's try search with functional_groups_broken ["acyl chloride"]? Actually sulfonyl chloride is not in list. Maybe use "sulfonamides" formed. Search for sulfonamide formation.
